## Which one doesn't belong? {#ss3-patterns .ap-lesson .ap-thinking}

<div class="ap-sequence-grid">
<div><strong class="ap-choice-number">1</strong><span data-math="5,8,11,14">5, 8, 11, 14</span></div>
<div><strong class="ap-choice-number">2</strong><span data-math="20,17,14,11">20, 17, 14, 11</span></div>
<div><strong class="ap-choice-number">3</strong><span data-math="7,7,7,7">7, 7, 7, 7</span></div>
<div><strong class="ap-choice-number">4</strong><span data-math="2,4,8,16">2, 4, 8, 16</span></div>
</div>

<div class="ap-thinking-prompts">
<div><h3>Claim</h3><p>Choose a sequence that does not belong.</p></div>
<div><h3>Support</h3><p>Give mathematical evidence for your choice.</p></div>
<div class="fragment" data-fragment-index="0"><h3>Question</h3><p>What question could you ask about someone else's claim?</p></div>
</div>

::: {.takeaway .fragment data-fragment-index="1"}
What property do 1, 2 and 3 share that 4 does not?

:::

::: notes

Allow about 3 minutes. Give students 20–30 seconds to choose and prepare evidence, then invite several claims. This is an open discussion, not a single-answer quiz. Accept different mathematically supported criteria.

Possible claims: 1 is the only list increasing by a constant amount. 2 is the only decreasing list. 3 is the only list with identical terms. 4 is the only list without a constant difference. Keep these possibilities in the notes so students produce their own arguments.

First click introduces Question. Ask partners to question a claim or its evidence. For example, if someone excludes 3 because it does not change, ask whether zero can still be a constant difference. Avoid announcing the arithmetic definition until the discussion has occurred.

Second click focuses the discussion on the shared property of 1, 2 and 3. Their consecutive differences are +3, −3 and 0 respectively. In 4 the differences are 2, 4 and 8. A finite prefix alone does not determine an infinite continuation.

Routine adapted from Project Zero, Harvard Graduate School of Education, Claim, Support, Question: https://www.pz.harvard.edu/resources/claim-support-question

:::
